migration.fingerprint_exclusion: Only the newly added serpapi_capable column; every existing value defaulted to false.

preserved.ssh_access: Original operator IPv4 /32 only; temporary deployment address removed.

connector.serpapi_key_location: Private environment of the operator's local connector only; not deployed or bundled.

checks: Both downloads and release manifest verified against local SHA-256 values over verified TLS.
Public health, owner setup and private files return 404; anonymous identity returns 401.
All three synthetic demo cases render read-only without document overflow or session cookies.
Owner password sign-in and logout retain Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict session protection.
Changing provider clears consent; an incapable worker is unavailable and rejected by the API.
Explicit SerpApi consent persists through native task dispatch, then cancellation before worker claim.
Missing explicit provider on follow-up returns 422; consented follow-up retains SerpApi and is cancelled before execution.
Research consent and follow-up forms fit desktop/mobile; mobile composer remains in normal flow.

local_validation.live_provider_scope: Successful persisted local SerpApi reports exist, but later attempts failed on unavailable captures or validation. The full paid browser journey was not recorded as passing. See docs/public-web-research.md.

limits: Hosted protocol checks are not proof of live hosted SerpApi research completion.
Real research requires the operator's current local connector, Codex access, private SerpApi key, explicit consent and provider credits.
No completed backup restore, renewed live-workload capacity test, full Google OAuth sign-in, or full hosted evidence-withdrawal test was performed in this release.
The prior API image cannot attest the migrated database; an image-only rollback is not valid.
The existing single-host Lightsail deployment remains a judging deployment, not a high-availability service.
